sentences.text: This petition under Section 166 MV Act is filed by the Petitioner seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.
2. It is stated that on 28-10-2023, at about 7:30 P.M., the petitioner was walking as a pedestrian at Nagamangala-Pandavapura Main Road, Near Thibbanakatte Bore, Ballale Village, Mandya District.
At that time, 3WLRGV goods auto-rickshaw bearing registration No. KA-11-5236 came in a rash and negligent manner and violently struck the petitioner.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Prajwal Hospital, Mysore, where the attending doctor advised urgent surgical intervention.
However, due to financial constraints, the petitioner had to return home.
After arranging the necessary funds, he was admitted for surgery on 30-10-2023 and remained under inpatient treatment till 31-10-2023.

3. The petitioner incurred an amount exceeding Rs. 1,00,000/- towards medical expenses,
conveyance, nourishment, and attendant charges.
Before the accident, the petitioner was a hale and healthy, earning up to Rs. 25,000/- per month.
Owing to the injuries sustained, he is now suffering from permanent disability, resulting in a substantial loss of earning capacity and future income.
4. The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, the petitioner prays that this Tribunal be pleased to award just and proper compensation against Respondent Nos. 1 and 2, being the owner and insurer of the said vehicle.
5. In response to the petition, Respondent No. 1 has appeared before this Court through counsel and filed a written statement.

Respondent No. 2 has not appeared despite service of notice and was accordingly placed ex parte.
6.
In its written statement, Respondent No. 1 - the Insurance Company - has denied all the material averments made in the petition.
It is specifically contended that the accident did not occur due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, but rather due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
It is further stated that the 3WLRGV goods auto- rickshaw, bearing Registration No. KA11 5236, was insured with this respondent under Policy No. VGTO269700000100, valid from 23.02.2023 to 24.02.2024.
Respondent No. 1 has disputed the nature and extent of injuries, the treatment undergone, income of the petitioner, the alleged disability, and the expenses incurred.

It is also contended that the compensation claimed is highly excessive and exaggerated, and as such,
the respondent has prayed for dismissal of the petition in toto.
7.

On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-

1. Whether the Petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries due to the actionable negligent driving of goods auto bearing Reg No.KA-11-5236 by its driver,
in RTA took place on 28.10.2023 at about 5.30 p.m on Nagamangala Pandavapura Main Road, Near Thibbanakattebore, Bellale Village, Mandya?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount and from whom?
3 . What order or award ?

8. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and in support of his case,
doctor is examined as PW-2 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.12.

On the other hand,
the Respondents have not chosen to adduce any oral and documentary evidence.

9. By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:

REASONS 10. ISSUE NO.1:- The case of the petitioner is that on 28-10-2023, at about 7:30 P.M., the petitioner was walking as a pedestrian at Nagamangala- Pandavapura Main Road, Near Thibbanakatte Bore,
Ballale Village, Mandya District.
At that time, 3WLRGV goods auto-rickshaw bearing registration No. KA-11- 5236 came in a rash and negligent manner and violently struck the petitioner.
As a result of the impact, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
He was immediately shifted to Prajwal Hospital, Mysore, where the attending doctor advised urgent surgical intervention.
However, due to financial constraints, the petitioner had to return home.

After arranging the necessary funds, he was admitted for surgery on 30- 10-2023 and remained under inpatient treatment till 31-10-2023..
11.

In order to substantiate his case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 7 i.e., FIR, complaint, petitioner statement, spot mahazar, charge sheet,
wound certificate and IMV report.

To support of his claim, Dr. B.Ramesh, Orthopedic surgeon is examined as PW-2 and he has produced the documents at Ex.P.11 and 12.
12.
As per EX P.6 wound certificate, the petitioner has sustained conscious oriented injury.
It is mentioned that the injury no.1 is grievous in nature.

13. The Respondent-Insurance Company has contended that the accident did not occur due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, but rather due to the negligence of the petitioner himself.
In support of this contention, certain suggestions were put forth during the cross-examination of the petitioner.

sentences.text: It was suggested to the petitioner that the alleged road did not have a footpath, which he denied.
He also denied the suggestion that there was no designated space for pedestrians on the said road and that the accident was caused due to his own negligence.
The petitioner deposed that he had seen the offending vehicle from a distance of approximately half a kilometre.
15. He denied the suggestion that he could have stood aside on the road to avoid the accident, and voluntarily stated that he had, in fact, stood aside.
He further denied the suggestion that if he had been more cautious while walking on the road, the accident could have been avoided.
The petitioner also denied the allegation that he lodged the complaint after three days of the incident because he had fallen on his own.
He refuted the suggestion that he had sustained only simple injuries without any bone fractures.

However, apart from these suggestions made during cross-examination and the general denials in the written statement, the Respondent has not produced any independent or corroborative evidence to establish that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner..
16. There is no material on record to disprove the evidence adduced by the petitioner or to substantiate the contentions raised by the respondent.
The testimony of PW1 is duly corroborated by the documentary evidence produced on record.
Nothing substantial has been elicited during cross-examination to discredit or shake the credibility of the petitioner's case.

17. It is a well-settled principle of law that the Motor Vehicles Act is a beneficial piece of legislation,
and the Claims Tribunal is not required to insist on strict proof of rashness and negligence as demanded in criminal trials.
In the present case, after due investigation, the police have filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle, which is marked as Exhibit P5.
This, along with other documentary evidence on record, prima facie establishes the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

Hence, based on the totality of the evidence, both oral and documentary, it is clearly established that the petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident caused solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle's driver.

Hence,
Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
18. ISSUE NO.2 :- As per Ex.P6, the wound certificate, the petitioner was conscious and oriented at the time of examination.
The Ex.P6 shows that Injury No. 1 as a grievous injury.

Due to the accident,
the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and was admitted as an inpatient and underwent surgical treatment in Prajwal hospital.
19. The petitioner has claimed to have incurred expenses exceeding 1,00,000 towards medical treatment, food, nourishment, conveyance, and other incidental charges.
20. PW2, Dr. B. Ramesh, Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru, deposed that the petitioner sustained a Galeazzi fracture and underwent internal fixation of the radius.

PW2 further stated that, upon clinical examination, the petitioner exhibited difficulty and restriction in joint movements of the left forearm, including pronation and supination, as well as difficulty in ambulation and lifting weight overhead with the left upper limb.

The muscle power of the left forearm was recorded at 4/5, compared to the normal 5/5.Radiological examination confirmed that Gangadhara B vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139410399/
4 the fracture had united with the implant in situ.

sentences.text:
Based on his clinical and radiological findings, PW2 assessed the permanent disability of the left upper limb at 26% and the whole body disability at 10%.
21.
In his cross-examination, PW2 clearly stated that he had not treated the petitioner personally.
His testimony is based on the verification of the wound certificate and discharge summary, without examination of the petitioner's earlier case sheets or clinical history.

It is pertinent to note that PW2 did not provide a specific opinion regarding functional disability, which relates to the practical impact of physical disability on the petitioner's ability to perform day-to-day activities and earn a livelihood.

Taking into consideration the nature and location of the injury, the degree of permanent disability sustained, its functional impact on the petitioner's daily and occasional activities, as well as the age and avocation of the petitioner, this Tribunal is of the considered view that the functional disability should be assessed at 6% to the whole body, as against 10% assessed purely on physical grounds.
This functional assessment is more appropriate for the purpose of computing compensation towards future loss of earning capacity.
22. In the petition, the age of the petitioner is mentioned as 36 years.
As per Exhibit P9 - Aadhaar Card, his year of birth is shown as 1987.
Accordingly, his age as on the date of the accident is considered as 36 years.

Therefore, the appropriate multiplier applicable to the case at hand is '15'.
23.
At the time of the accident, the petitioner was working as a coolie and claimed to be earning a sum of Rs. 25,000 per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident, he has suffered permanent disability, resulting in loss of earning capacity and future income.
24. However, the petitioner has not produced any documentary evidence to substantiate his occupation or income.

In the absence of proof of income, this Tribunal deems it appropriate to assess the income based on the notional income guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority As the accident occurred in the year 2023, the notional income is taken as Rs.
16,000 per month for the purpose of computation of compensation.
25.

Thus this tribunal is of the opinion that the petitioner who sustained the injuries is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
26. Loss of future income on account of permanent disability:
Considering the petitioner's grievous injury which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, this court is of the opinion that the functional disability of 6% is reasonable and just.
27. The petitioner was 36 years old as on date of alleged accident and the multiplier applicable to the petitioner as per decision laid down by Hon'ble Apex court in Sarla Verma's case is at 15.
The notional income taken as Rs.16,000 x 12 x 15 x 6/100= Rs.1,72,800/- towards loss of future income.
28. Pain and sufferings:

So far as the compensation under non-pecuniary damages are concerned,
considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in performing daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of inpatient treatment and physical and mental suffering endured by the petitioner, this tribunal is of the opinion that an amount of .30,000/- would be just and fair Gangadhara B vs Royal Sun All Ins Co Ltd on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139410399/
5 compensation under head of Pain and sufferings 29.

sentences.text: Loss of amenities of life:
undoubtedly the petitioner is suffering from difficulties in performing day to day activities and is facing continuous hardship due to the disability.
Therefore this tribunal finds to appropriate to award a sum .25,000/- under head of loss of amenities of life.
30. Medical expenses:
Under the pecuniary damages, expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization and medicines, the Petitioner has produced medical bills at Ex.P.10 amounting to Rs.36,899/-.
There is no evidence forthcoming to disbelieve the said medical bills.
On perusal of medical bills, it appears that the petitioner has spent Rs.36,899 /- towards medical treatment.
The medical bills appears to be genuine.
Therefore, the Petitioner is awarded compensation of .36,899/- towards Medical Expenses.
31. Future medical expenses:
PW-2 has stated that the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implant.
But he has not produced any estimation.

Considering the potential future surgery, this tribunal is of the opinion that it would be just and reasonable to award Rs.15,000/-
towards under head of future medical expenses.
32. Conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges:
Ex.P.8 -Discharge summary shows that Petitioner was admitted at Nagarajegowda Memorial Hospital Mysore, as an inpatient from 30.10.2023 to 03.11.2023 i.e., totally for a period of 5 days.
Therefore, it is just and reasonable to award compensation of .10,000/- under the head of conveyance, food, nourishment and attendant charges.
33. Loss of earning during laid up period:

With regard to the loss of earnings during treatment period, Considering the nature of the grievous injury, which has resulted in significant difficulty in carrying out daily vocational activities, as well as the duration of impatient treatment and recovery,
this tribunal considers the 2 months for rest is considered .

As the monthly income of the Petitioner is already considered as .16,000/- per month, loss of earning during laid up period would be .16,000 x 2 = Rs.32,000/-.
34.

Thus the compensation awarded under the various heads are as under:

4. Medical expenses  36,899/-

In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos. 1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Draw award accordingly.
